scene.note: Callbacks always run after the current code, in one order, and the price list can ask for many things at once.

steps.note: The invite count comes from memory, so its docket is already kept when then() is called.
then() does not run the callback now. It queues it to run once the code that is running has finished.
The line under then() runs first, every night, whether the count was in memory or not.
Then the queued callbacks run, before any timer, in the order their then() calls were made.
The price list asks for three counts at once and hands all three dockets to Docket.all().
The answers come back in any order. Each one goes to the place of its own docket, and Docket.all() counts them.

value.label: values, in the order of the list

steps.note: When the last one arrives, the counts go out in the order they were asked for. One failure would end it at once.
The price list races the press queue against a docket that fails after half a second.
Whichever settles first settles the race. The other changes nothing.
Idris gets the first free day, or a sentence saying the queue did not answer in time.
